title: Connected to router but no internet
causes: The router is reachable but has no internet.
Internet service is down.
steps: Check if a phone or laptop can get online on the same network.
If nothing is online, call your internet provider.
If other devices work, restart the TV.
Restart the router and modem, then reconnect.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wired network connection problem
causes: The Ethernet cable is loose or faulty.
The router port is not working.
steps: Push the Ethernet cable firmly into the TV and the router.
Try a different cable or router port.
Restart the TV, then the router and modem.
Try Wi-Fi briefly to see if the internet itself works.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wired connection cannot reach internet
causes: The router has no internet.
The Ethernet cable is not seated well.
steps: Check that another device is online.
If yes, restart the TV.
If not, unplug and replug the Ethernet cable at both ends.
Restart the router before calling your provider.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Cannot connect to the wireless network
causes: Wrong network name chosen.
Wrong password typed.
Router or TV needs a restart.
steps: Check you picked the right network name.
Re-type the password; it is case-sensitive.
Restart the TV and the router.
Try connecting again.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Weak Wi-Fi signal blocks connection
causes: The TV is too far from the router.
Walls or objects weaken the signal.
steps: Move the TV or router closer, or raise the router.
Restart the router and the TV.
If your router has two bands, try the other one.
Reconnect to the network.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wi-Fi connection failed, weak signal
causes: Weak Wi-Fi signal.
Temporary router or TV glitch.
steps: Restart the router and the TV.
Move the TV closer to the router.
Reconnect to Wi-Fi.
Try the other router band if available.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wrong password or router restriction
causes: The Wi-Fi password was typed wrongly.
The router blocks unknown devices.
steps: Check the network name and re-enter the password.
If the router filters devices, add the TV's wireless MAC address.
Restart the TV and the router.
Try again.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wrong password or router restriction

The router blocks unknown devices.
steps: Check the network name and re-enter the password carefully.
If the router filters devices, allow the TV's wireless MAC address.
Restart the TV and the router.
Try again.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Connection lost while opening a channel
causes: The network dropped while an app was starting.
Weak Wi-Fi signal.
steps: Choose Set up connection on screen and follow the prompts.
Restart the TV and the router.
Check the Wi-Fi signal strength.
Move the TV and router closer.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Poor wireless signal strength
causes: Weak Wi-Fi signal at the TV.
Obstacles between TV and router.
steps: Move the TV and router closer together.
Clear obstacles between them.
Restart the TV and the router.
Use an Ethernet cable if the TV has a port.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Internet speed too slow
causes: Your internet plan or line is slow.
Other devices use the bandwidth.
steps: Pause downloads and streams on other devices.
Restart the modem and router.
Ask your provider what speed you get.
Consider a faster plan.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Wireless connection failure
causes: Temporary Wi-Fi fault between the TV and the router.
steps: Restart the router and wait for it to come back online.
Restart the Roku TV.
Try connecting to the network again.
Move the TV closer if the signal is weak.
technician: If the error keeps returning after these steps, contact Roku support or your internet provider.

title: Sony TV detected a fault (2 blinks)
causes: The TV found an internal fault.
The meaning of the blink count differs between models.
steps: Switch off and unplug the TV for 1 minute, away from any power strip.
Clear the vents so air can flow.
Unplug all connected devices and switch on again.
Update the TV software if it starts.
Note the blink count and contact Sony.
technician: Most red blink faults need service, so contact Sony support with the blink count.

title: Sleep or on/off timer is active
causes: A sleep timer or on/off timer is set on the TV.
steps: Open the TV Settings menu.
Find the sleep timer or on/off timer.
Turn the timer off or change the time.
Check the light goes out.
technician: No service is needed unless the light stays on with no timer set.

title: Software update running or cable loose
causes: A software update is in progress.
On sets with a separate media box, the cable between the units may be loose.
steps: Do not switch off or unplug the TV; wait a few minutes.
The remote will not work during the update.
On media box sets, check the cable between the units is firm.
technician: If it blinks for a long time, contact Sony support.

title: Normal start-up or TV will not start
causes: Normal while the TV powers on.
Possible fault if it never stops or the TV cycles on and off.
steps: Wait for the TV to finish starting; the blinking should stop.
If it keeps blinking, unplug the TV for 3 minutes.
Plug in and try again.
technician: If the TV still will not start, it needs service from Sony.

title: Projection TV lamp needs replacing
causes: The lamp has burned out (projection TVs and projectors only).
The lamp cover may be open.
steps: Switch off and let the lamp cool.
Make sure the lamp covers are closed and secure.
Do not touch the lamp glass; wipe it with an alcohol wipe if touched.
Arrange a lamp replacement.
technician: Contact Sony support to get a replacement lamp.

title: Fault shown by repeating red blinks
causes: The TV found a fault and shows a flash count.
steps: Count the flashes between each pause.
Unplug the TV, wait 2 minutes, plug in and switch on.
If it repeats, unplug and call Sony with the flash count.
technician: Give the flash count to Sony support.

title: TV detected an error (SOS)
causes: The TV found an internal error.
Applies to Panasonic Fire TV models.
steps: Unplug the TV for a few minutes.
Plug it back in and switch on.
If it still blinks, send a repair request to Panasonic.
technician: If blinking continues, submit a repair support request to Panasonic.

title: Standby while panel maintenance or network task runs
causes: Panel maintenance or a network function is in progress.
steps: Do not touch or press the screen during panel maintenance.
Wait until the task finishes.
Read the Panasonic panel maintenance article if it repeats.
technician: If the light stays orange for a long time, contact Panasonic support.

title: Panel maintenance or network update running
causes: Panel maintenance is running.
A network connection or settings update is in progress.
steps: Leave the TV plugged in and wait for it to finish.
If the LED turns orange again after you switch the TV on or off, maintenance is not done.
Let it complete before switching off.
technician: If it never stops, contact Panasonic support.

title: TV starting or waiting for Bluetooth pairing
causes: The TV is starting up.
It is waiting for a Bluetooth device to pair.
steps: Wait for start-up to finish.
If pairing, complete pairing on the other device.
Unplug briefly and retry if it never stops.
technician: If the TV never finishes starting, contact Panasonic support.

title: Philips TV reports a fault
causes: The TV has detected a fault.
The TV may have overheated.
steps: Unplug the TV from the wall outlet.
Let it cool down fully.
Plug the power cable back in.
Switch it on again.
technician: If the red light blinks again, contact Philips Consumer Care.

code: Front LED blinks in a repeating pattern
title: TV will not start, LED blinks repeatedly
causes: The TV does not start and shows no picture or sound.
A temporary power glitch.
steps: Do a power cycle: unplug the TV and wait a few minutes.
Plug in and try again.
Try a different wall socket.
technician: If it still blinks, contact Philips TV support.

title: TV not connected to the network
causes: The TV has no working internet connection.
The Wi-Fi adapter or router settings are not suitable.
steps: Test another device on the same network.
Restart the router and the TV, then re-enter the Wi-Fi password.
In Wi-Fi advanced settings, set DNS manually to 8.8.8.8.
Use 5 GHz if the TV supports it and move the router closer.
technician: If nothing works, the Wi-Fi module may need replacing, so contact LG service.
